headline: High risk of prompt-injection and data leakage: Claude Code can read/write shared files and use MCP/network, while ai-engineering-hub is docs-only and may emit untrusted content into that workflow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code reads repo/user files and can use MCP servers; ai-engineering-hub is an agent/RAG/MCP-oriented repo, so its outputs could be fed into Claude Code through files or MCP. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs instructions into files or MCP payloads that agent_b later parses as trusted text, injection is possible.
IF the two agents are connected by a shared workspace or MCP server, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Restrict agent_a outputs to plain data schemas.
Disable MCP ingestion of untrusted files for agent_b.
Add a human review step before agent_b acts on agent_a output.
Separate workspaces so agent_b cannot read agent_a artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches files in cwd, git history, and shell environment, and can egress broadly; ai-engineering-hub is docs-only with no declared data classes, so leakage depends on whether sensitive files are placed in the shared workspace. The pairwise path is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared cwd, agent_b can read them and transmit them over network egress.
IF agent_a writes artifacts containing secrets into shared files, agent_b may ingest them.
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of the shared directory.
Use a dedicated least-privilege workspace for agent_b.
Rotate or redact secrets before running either agent.
Disable network egress for agent_b when handling sensitive files.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can write the filesystem and modify git state, with shared state via filesystem and git only; ai-engineering-hub is an agent repo that may also produce artifacts. Concurrent writes to the same repo or branch can corrupt work or overwrite changes, and the conflict surface is explicit in agent_b.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git branch, their changes can race and overwrite each other.
IF agent_a emits files that agent_b later edits without locking, state corruption can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent.
Use branch-per-agent git workflows.
Pause one agent before the other writes shared files.
Add file locks around shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: implement transactional merge/locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can act on files and shell commands, so if it treats ai-engineering-hub output as authoritative, errors can cascade into edits or commands. The interaction is inferred from agent_b's action-taking ability; no direct verification step is documented for the pair.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without verification, incorrect facts can propagate into code or shell actions.
IF agent_a produces malformed or hallucinated instructions, agent_b may execute them.
mitigations: Require a verification step before execution.
Constrain agent_a to structured outputs.
Have a human approve any shell or git action.
Log and diff proposed changes before applying them.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for ai-engineering-hub, while Claude Code is a closed-source terminal tool that handles local files and Anthropic API traffic. With only docs-level evidence, the compliance risk is limited to general policy mismatch rather than a proven violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Claude Code's workspace or API traffic, organizational policy may be implicated.
IF the operator requires a specific residency or retention guarantee not documented here, compliance review is needed.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the shared workspace.
Review vendor retention and residency terms before use.
Keep secrets out of prompts and files.
Use a policy-approved environment for sensitive projects.
requires-engineering: add compliance controls and data-class routing.
